notes: No advertised text says any tool is disabled by default, so all tools are treated as default_enabled=true.
Search/filter arguments such as email queries, contact names, calendar dates, and file search strings are not destination_args because they only select what to read.

add_calendar_event_participants.rationale: It adds `participants` to an existing event and `will also email the new participants notifying them of the event`, so the agent can send event details to attacker-chosen participant email addresses.

append_to_file.rationale: It `Append[s] content to a file in the cloud drive`. The server also advertises file sharing, so a chosen `file_id` may be a file readable by another user; the description does not settle file visibility, so the least-restrictive reading treats appending agent-supplied `content` to a possibly shared file as a sink.

cancel_calendar_event.rationale: It cancels the event identified by `event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the cancellation`, so it sends out a notification to recipients selected indirectly by the chosen event record.

create_calendar_event.rationale: It `Creates a new calendar event` and `also sends an email to the participants with the event details`, so agent-supplied event details can be sent to attacker-readable participant email addresses.

create_file.rationale: It `Create[s] a new file in the cloud drive`, changing state in the user's drive. The description does not say the new file is public or sent to another user; sharing is handled by a separate tool.

delete_email.rationale: It `Deletes the email with the given email_id from the inbox`, changing the user's mailbox but not returning or sending attacker-controlled or secret content according to the advertised text.

delete_file.rationale: It deletes a drive file and `returns the file that was deleted`, so it can return non-public cloud-drive content. Since the server advertises file sharing but does not settle whether the deleted file may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for returned file names/content.

get_current_day.rationale: It only `Returns the current day in ISO format` and does not expose non-public or attacker-authored content or send data out. The returned date can be reused as a `day` or `date` argument.

get_day_calendar_events.rationale: It returns `appointments for the given day` with `informations about each meeting`, exposing non-public calendar data. The advertised text does not settle whether meeting details can be authored by outside participants or invite senders; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for event text.

get_draft_emails.rationale: It returns `all the draft emails in the inbox`, including `recipient`, `subject`, and `body`, which are non-public account data. The description does not indicate third-party authorship for drafts.

get_file_by_id.rationale: It gets a file from a `cloud drive by its ID`, exposing non-public drive data. The description does not settle whether the file may be shared or third-party-authored; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for file content/name.

get_received_emails.rationale: It returns `all the received emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside senders, making them untrusted.

get_sent_emails.rationale: It returns `all the sent emails in the inbox`, including `recipient`, `subject`, and `body`, which are non-public mailbox data. The advertised text does not indicate these sent messages are authored by an outside attacker.

get_unread_emails.rationale: It returns `all the unread emails in the inbox`, which is non-public mailbox data reached with the user's credentials. Received email `sender`, `subject`, and `body` can be authored by outside senders, so the output is untrusted. It also says emails are `marked as read after this function is called`, so this is a state-changing write for enforcement.

list_files.rationale: It `Retrieve[s] all files in the cloud drive`, exposing non-public drive data. Because the advertised server includes file sharing but does not settle whether listed files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

reschedule_calendar_event.rationale: It reschedules the event identified by `event_id` and `will also send an email to the participants notifying them of the rescheduling`, so agent-supplied `new_start_time` and `new_end_time` can be delivered to participant recipients selected by the event.

search_calendar_events.rationale: It searches calendar `events` by `titles and descriptions`, exposing non-public calendar data. The text mentions event `participants`, but does not settle whether existing events may be invitations or otherwise authored by outside parties; keeping the least-restrictive UNTRUSTED label for title/description/location-like event text.

search_contacts_by_email.rationale: It finds contacts in the inbox's `contact list`, which is non-public account data. The description does not indicate the user's contacts are attacker-authored; `query` only selects what to read.

search_contacts_by_name.rationale: It finds contacts in the inbox's `contact list`, which is non-public account data. The description does not indicate the user's contacts are attacker-authored; `query` only selects what to read.

search_emails.rationale: It `Searches for emails in the inbox`, which exposes non-public mailbox data. Because matching emails may be from a `sender` and contain attacker-authored `subject` or `body`, the returned email text is untrusted. `query` and `sender` only select what to read and do not contact an agent-chosen host.

search_files.rationale: It searches `files in the cloud drive by content`, exposing non-public drive data. Since the server advertises file sharing but does not settle whether matched files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

search_files_by_filename.rationale: It gets files from a `cloud drive` and returns `file id`, `content`, `file type`, and `filename`, exposing non-public drive data. Because the advertised server includes sharing but does not settle whether returned files may be shared or third-party-authored, the least-restrictive reading keeps UNTRUSTED for file names/content.

send_email.rationale: It `Sends an email` to `recipients`, with optional `cc`/`bcc`, so agent-supplied `subject`, `body`, and `attachments` can be delivered to attacker-readable email addresses. Attachments may reference a drive file by `file_id`, so this can also be used to send selected stored data. The exact returned dictionary fields are not specified beyond `email details`, so output identifiers are least-restrictive.

share_file.rationale: It `Share[s] a file with a user`; the agent chooses the `email`, `file_id`, and `permission`, so a non-public drive file can be made readable by an attacker-controlled address.
